headline: Camera-Based Traffic Enforcement Returns in Manila, Quezon City, San Juan, Muntinlupa and Parañaque
seoTitle: NCAP Returns in Five Metro Manila Cities
seoDescription: The No Contact Apprehension Policy resumes on October 5 in five Metro Manila cities. Valenzuela deferred its restart because of road repairs.
deck: Valenzuela put its own restart on hold because of road repairs. Fines follow the Metro Manila Traffic Code of 2023, according to reports.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: The No Contact Apprehension Policy resumes on Monday, October 5, in Manila, Muntinlupa, Parañaque, Quezon City and San Juan, according to Rappler, the Inquirer and GMA News. Quezon City's own announcement also sets the reimplementation date at October 5.
Valenzuela had planned to restart on the same day but deferred because of ongoing road repairs and changing traffic conditions.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Under NCAP, CCTV and other cameras record suspected violations and notices go to the registered vehicle owner without an enforcer stopping the vehicle. Reports say violations are reviewed before notices are issued. Rappler reports that motorists can receive real-time notices by SMS and email and can check recorded violations on the "May Huli Ka" website and in the eGovPH app.

Fines follow the Metro Manila Traffic Code of 2023, the Inquirer reports. People who believe they were wrongly apprehended can contest through designated online channels. The PNP said it is ready to help local governments enforce the policy. Rappler says the MMDA has used NCAP on some major roads since May 2025.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Registered owners in the five cities can receive camera notices. Rappler says they can also check records on the "May Huli Ka" website and the eGovPH app.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: No new start date for Valenzuela had been reported by Monday afternoon.
